reasons.D: First-person present with short declaratives, quiet fragments and a dry half-admission ('Or not only.'); it closes on a still, inventory-like picture of things put away, which is the passage's movement and stance.
reasons.B: Also first-person present with short, plain sentences and the right rhythm, but it slips into a mildly instructive tone ('This is where people go wrong') and leans on 'Then...' openers more mechanically than the author does.
reasons.C: It has the choppy rhythm but is written mostly as imperatives to 'you', a manual voice the author never uses. The stacked one-word fragments and asides ('Nobody likes this part.') overdo the terseness to the point of caricature.
reasons.A: Long, clause-heavy sentences joined with 'and', 'because' and participial openers, in a smooth explanatory register. This is far from the author's clipped, paratactic movement.
